summary: Discusses implementation techniques for tunneling with IP protocol number 4 encapsulation, particularly with IP Security and other protocols. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Putting a whole packet inside another packet like a letter in an envelope, so it can travel through places that couldn't carry it alone.

questions: what is ip in ip tunneling
how does mtu discovery work in tunnels
subtitle: Encapsulating IP packets inside IP packets to bridge networks.

tldr.problem: Networks sometimes have incompatible policies or capabilities, making direct communication impossible. Sites need a way to send IP packets across such boundaries.
tldr.mechanism: IP in IP tunneling adds an outer IP header to an existing IP packet, creating a wrapper that traverses the intermediate network. The original packet arrives unchanged at the tunnel exit.
tldr.outcome: This simple technique has been used for decades in amateur radio networks and early IP Security implementations to bridge incompatible network segments without protocol changes.

today: RFC 1853 is informational and remains historically significant. IP in IP tunneling continues to be used in certain contexts, though modern networks often employ more sophisticated tunneling protocols like GRE or VPN technologies. The techniques for tunnel management and ICMP error handling described here remain relevant for any tunneling implementation.

sections.title: Introduction and History
sections.content:
RFC 1853 documents IP in IP tunneling, a long-standing practice for bridging network segments with incompatible policies or capabilities. The technique uses IP Protocol Number 4 to encapsulate one IP packet inside another.

The RFC notes that this approach differs from later tunneling techniques (such as GRE, which uses protocol number 47). IP in IP tunneling does not insert special headers between the inner and outer IP headers; it simply wraps the original IP header and payload in a new outer IP header. The technique has been used by the Amateur Packet Radio network for mobile networking and by early IP Security implementations.
sections.eli5: When a packet needs to cross through a network that does not understand it, you wrap it in another header that the intermediate network does understand.

sections.title: How Encapsulation Works
sections.content:
Encapsulation is straightforward: an outer IP header is prepended to the original IP packet. Optionally, tunnel-specific headers (such as security headers) can be inserted between the outer and inner headers.

The outer IP header's source and destination addresses identify the tunnel endpoints (the encapsulator and decapsulator). The inner IP header's source and destination addresses identify the original sender and recipient. The outer header's protocol field indicates what follows (protocol 4 if the inner header is IP with no intervening headers).

Several encapsulation rules apply. The Type of Service (TOS) field is copied from the inner header, preserving quality-of-service intent. A new Identification number is generated for the outer header (since the encapsulated datagram may already be fragmented, and tunnel fragmentation happens at a different level). The Don't Fragment bit is copied from the inner header, allowing the originator to control fragmentation behavior. The TTL is set to a default value, then decremented by the originator before encapsulation. The inner TTL is decremented once and not affected by decapsulation. Options are not copied from the inner header, as they may not apply to the tunnel path.
sections.eli5: The outer header wraps the original packet and contains the addresses of the tunnel entry and exit points, while the inner header retains the original source and destination.

sections.title: Managing Tunnel State
sections.content:
The RFC emphasizes that routers must carefully maintain soft state about their tunnels. When a router inside the tunnel encounters an error, it sends an ICMP message back to the encapsulator. However, ICMP normally only includes 64 bits of the problematic datagram beyond the IP header, which is not enough to include the entire encapsulated header. By maintaining soft state, the encapsulator can infer the tunnel condition and send accurate ICMP messages to the originating host.

The router should track at least three pieces of soft state: reachability of the tunnel endpoint, congestion of the tunnel, and the MTU (maximum transmission unit) of the tunnel. When a datagram arrives that would violate the tunnel state (for example, a packet larger than the tunnel MTU when Don't Fragment is set), the router sends an appropriate ICMP error to the originator but also forwards the datagram into the tunnel to learn about state changes.
sections.eli5: The tunnel entry point keeps track of whether the tunnel is working, whether it is congested, and how big packets can be. When something goes wrong inside the tunnel, the entry point figures out what happened and tells the original sender.

sections.title: Error Handling and Special Cases
sections.content:
The RFC discusses several specific error conditions and how tunnels should handle them.

Path MTU Discovery: When the Don't Fragment bit is set, proper tunnel MTU discovery depends on ICMP "Datagram Too Big" errors. All tunnel implementations must support Path MTU Discovery. Fragmentation caused by encapsulation overhead happens only once after encapsulation, improving efficiency.

Congestion: Tunnel soft state collects congestion indications such as ICMP Source Quench messages from the tunnel peer. When forwarding another datagram into the tunnel, the encapsulator should send Source Quench to the originator.

Routing loops: Because TTL is reset each time a datagram is encapsulated, routing loops are particularly dangerous if the packet arrives again at the encapsulator. An implementation must not further encapsulate if the IP source matches any of the encapsulator's interfaces. ICMP Time Exceeded messages report loops within the tunnel; Destination Unreachable messages report delivery failures to the decapsulator, which should be reported as Network Unreachable.

Other ICMP messages: Parameter problem messages are likely to result from encapsulator misconfiguration and must not be reported to the originator.
sections.eli5: If the tunnel gets clogged, breaks, or creates a loop, special rules handle how to tell the original sender about the problem.
